Ah, yes, tnx. I saw that somewhere. Which is the real problem: where can I read about deploying helm packages idempotently with the same command. It's not in the documentation.

Is anybody reading this with the know how to edit the docs about this? I suspect ppl are losing time finding out about this, like me.

@Morriz the documentation is available [in the docs/ section](https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/tree/master/docs) of the codebase. If you file a PR to amend the documentation, https://docs.helm.sh/ will be updated.

Yes, but imo these intructions should come as close to, or even replace the original instructions in ‘using helm’, because I think helm should advocate a stateless approach. issue.title: helm upgrade --install no longer works
issue.body: As of helm v2.7.1, after updating tiller, running helm upgrade --install flag no longer works. The following error is displayed: Error: UPGRADE FAILED: "${RELEASE}" has no deployed releases. Downgrading to v2.7.0 or v2.6.2 does not produce the error.

body:
We are getting this with 2.8.2 when using `upgrade --install`. Regression?

```
$ helm upgrade --values values.yml --timeout 300 --namespace=production --wait --install --force ftp-server-production ftp-server-production

$ helm ls ftp-server

10      	Wed Mar 28 14:28:58 2018	PENDING_UPGRADE	ftp-server-0.0.1	Preparing upgrade
```

How to get it unstuck?

does it work if you specify the release name:
helm upgrade ftp-server-production --values values.yml --timeout 300 --namespace production --wait --install --force ftp-server-production

Unfortunately, I deleted the release as there was some urgency involved. (Of course, this caused me bunch of extra work, since I now had to reattach a PVC and load balancer manually etc., since Helm doesn't seem to have a way to remove a release but preserve the current resources. Ugh.)

I tried manually rewriting history by deleting the configmap corresponding to the release and restarting Tiller. I also tried a rollback, which worked, but the next deploy failed with the same error.

How does specifying the release name affect things? Doesn't it just default to what's in `Chart.yaml`?
@splisson-altair Actually, I see now that we do pass both the release name and the chart path. Not sure why that didn't get included in my paste. (Will edit.)
usually if I have some issue like that with a release, I do: helm delete <release> --purge
That's what I did. This is highly undesirable, as it deletes some state such as the connection between services and load balancers, or PVCs with their PVs.
I'm getting this on a lot of deploys now. Until this is fixed, is there a temporary workaround *aside* from `helm delete --purge`?
Note this is currently happening for a deploy that is currently in the `DEPLOYED` state. The one I pasted about above was stuck in `PENDING_UPGRADE`. So it seems unrelated to status.
